subject: Hospitality
title: Psychological Pricing in Hospitality
description: A 60-second lesson on Psychological Pricing in Hospitality.

hook.text: A room priced at $199 feels significantly cheaper than one at $200—even though the difference is just $1. Pricing is psychology.

buildup.text: Hotels use 'charm pricing' (ending in 9), 'prestige pricing' (round numbers for luxury).

discovery.text: Showing three options—budget, standard, premium—pushes most guests toward the middle. This is called the 'decoy effect.'

twist.text: Removing the dollar sign from hotel restaurant menus increases spending by 8–12%. The symbol triggers price awareness.

climax.text: Every price in a hotel is engineered: minibar items, spa treatments, room rates. Nothing is accidental; everything is strategy.

punchline.text: $199 beats $200. Remove the dollar sign. Pricing is a science of perception.

quiz.question: What is the 'decoy effect' in pricing?
options: Showing three options where the middle one seems like the best deal
